text:
Carla Mendoza: Heads up — UI shows p95 > p99 for /v1/generate in eu-west since ~14:30. p95=240ms, p99=180ms. Screenshot attached? (I'll upload)
Ben Li: whoa that's... wrong. p95 can't be higher than p99 unless sample set changed. Did something change in backend aggregator?
Alice Park: I noticed odd percentiles in canary yesterday but dismissed as sampling noise. Same endpoint?
Carla Mendoza: yes, same endpoint. Only EU region. US looks fine.
Dave R.: @metrics-bot any deploys around 14:25 that touched tdigest merge code?
metrics-bot: deploy metrics-aggregator v2.3.1 to eu-west at 14:22 by @ci. Release notes: "optimize merge path, preserve sample-count metadata".
Erin O'Neil: Release note says preserve sample-count, but maybe tags got dropped and weights zeroed out during merge.
Ben Li: If we merge two t-digests with inconsistent sample counts, the merged percentiles could invert. Unlikely but possible.
Alice Park: Repro steps: query raw metric stream for /v1/generate with 1s window and dump raw latencies. I can run a small job.
Carla Mendoza: Also the dashboard shows sample count 3 for p99 and 200 for p95 in the same time slice. That mismatch is probably the clue.
Dave R.: ah — sample-origin mismatch. Looks like p99 is computed on a different sampled subset (gateway-level) while p95 uses route-level aggregated data. If legends mixed origins when we roll up across routes, UI could show both numbers side-by-side incorrectly.
Ben Li: So the UI is merging metrics from different provenance without exposing origin. The backend returns a map like {p50:..., p95:..., p99:...} with no origin tag. Frontend just renders.
Erin O'Neil: Suggestion: add provenance tag to each percentile line and hide values when provenance differs across quantiles. Short-term: add guard that if sample_count variance > 100x, flag the tile.
Alice Park: Quick reproduction command I used:
```
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/query?metric=latency&endpoint=/v1/generate&region=eu-west&window=60s" | jq .
```
Look for fields "sample_count" per-quantile.
Carla Mendoza: I ran that and got:
`{"p50":30,"p95":240,"p99":180, "p50_count":210, "p95_count":3, "p99_count":3}`
Ben Li: Yep, UI showing raw numbers without counts is the UX bug.
Kate (SRE): For immediate mitigation we can patch console to show counts next to percentiles and add a tooltip: "Different sample sets; compare with caution". I'll open an infra ticket.
Carla Mendoza: Also posting because routing policy change two hours earlier bumped fallback weight to v2-lite. That might change which exporter tags the request.
Dave R.: Good call. If fallback routes hit a different exporter (gateway vs node), then provenance tag won't match. We should require exporter provenance in telemetry schema v3.
Erin O'Neil: Plan: 1) Alice to run a backfill job for 2 hours to confirm scope (in progress). 2) Kate to create infra ticket to add provenance to API + hotfix for console to surface counts. 3) Ben/Dave to review aggregator merge semantics for tdigest. 4) Carla to notify PMs that dashboard numbers for EU /v1/generate may be misleading.
Ben Li: I'll start a quick PR to show counts & dim percentiles with count < 10.
metrics-bot: incident created: MI-2026-041 — "eu-west latency percentile provenance mismatch" by @Kate (SRE)
Carla Mendoza: Thanks folks. If anyone spots similar inversion elsewhere, ping this thread. :eyes: 
Alice Park: Backfill found same inversion from 14:18–14:40, limited to calls where fallback weight > 0. Sending paste of raw json to the ticket.
Dave R.: moving to follow-up channel after lunch. TL;DR: not a math bug in percentile calc, it's a provenance/sampling/merge/display mismatch. UI guard should prevent confusion.
Carla Mendoza: closing loop: temporary fix merged to console canary. PR: #9723. Rollout at 16:10. Monitor pctl numbers.
Ben Li: monitoring alert rule added: if p95 > p99 for any endpoint -> auto mute tile + slack notify eng-platform.
Kate (SRE): Nice. We'll track MI-2026-041 until full telemetry schema v3 is live.
